title: Decide first whether it is an attempt
statement: Decide first whether an answer is a real attempt: never grade nonsense, a joke or a refusal, and if no attempt comes, end with a model answer.
detail: A 3D version's closing debate and its end-of-lesson reflection both tell the model to decide first whether the answer is a real attempt, any claim however rough, and to treat nonsense, 'idk', a single unrelated word, a joke or a refusal as no attempt, never pretending it is one and never calling it honest. A non-attempt is never quoted or praised: the debate says plainly that there is no position yet and asks again, and if neither answer is an attempt it closes with a model position, because the student must leave with an answer to the question. A live test of the paragraph task checks that nonsense is shown beside the model answer on return, not filed as plain secure.
against: The reading checkpoint in the same build does not keep this apart: after a second try that is not secure it sets the verdict to secure (`othello-archive/src/steps/Reading.tsx`, line 156) and shows "✓ Accepted" under the answer (`othello-archive/src/ui.tsx`, line 99), so a second nonsense answer is shown as accepted.

evidence.quote: Nonsense, "idk", a single unrelated word, a joke or a refusal is NOT an attempt. Never pretend it is one, and never call it honest.
The student must leave with an answer to the question.
First decide: is the answer NOW a real attempt at the learning question (any claim about it, however rough)? Nonsense, "idk", a single unrelated word or a refusal is not.
If it is not an attempt: do not quote it and do not comment on it.
l1-ind on return: nonsense shown beside the model, not filed as plain secure
**Refusals are acknowledged, never graded** (PRA-143). A refusal spends the attempt but is not "wrong"; zero quality credit, warm ack, beat completes.
Refusals are recognized locally (acknowledged, never judged).
